messages.content: We are ready to start comparing the Gulf Coast stay. The two possible windows are Sunday, August 3 through Friday, August 8, or Sunday, August 10 through Friday, August 15. It will be me, my spouse, and our 14-year-old daughter, and we will drive from Dallas once we settle on the lodging.

I can compare five-night stays in three formats: a beachfront hotel with direct sand access, a condominium with more interior space, and a hotel across the road from the beach. Before I price representative options, do you want one room in the hotels, and does the condominium need two actual bedrooms or would one bedroom plus a sleeper sofa work?

One hotel room is fine if it has two real beds. For the condo, compare a two-bedroom unit. I do not want the headline nightly rate unless you also show parking, cleaning, resort or destination fees, and occupancy taxes.

Understood. I will use one room with two queen beds for the hotels and a two-bedroom condominium for three guests. I will separate every mandatory charge and treat refundable deposits as holds rather than lodging cost. Should I keep this to Orange Beach and Gulf Shores, or include Fort Morgan?
Keep it to Orange Beach and Gulf Shores. We do not know which one we want yet.

For a representative direct-beach hotel, Best Western Premier The Tides in Orange Beach has a two-queen room showing in both windows. August 3-8 is $1,645 room charge, $263.20 lodging and occupancy taxes, and $50 parking, for $1,958.20 total. August 10-15 is $1,745 room charge, $279.20 taxes, and $50 parking, for $2,074.20. There is no separate cleaning or resort fee in either quote. The property is directly on the sand.
That is a useful baseline. What does the condo look like once the fees are included?

A two-bedroom, two-bath unit at Phoenix VII in Orange Beach is available August 3-8. Its breakdown is $1,450 rent, $185 departure cleaning, $75 reservation fee, $55 for one parking pass, and $237.60 in lodging and occupancy taxes, totaling $2,002.60. There is no additional resort fee. A $300 refundable damage hold is required but is not included in that total.
Is that exact condo available the second week too?

No. That exact unit is blocked beginning August 11, so it cannot cover August 10-15. A comparable two-bedroom in the same building is available for the second window at $1,525 rent, $195 cleaning, $75 reservation fee, $55 parking, and $248 lodging and occupancy taxes. Its mandatory total is $2,098. The replacement has a side-facing balcony rather than the first unit's front-facing balcony.
So the condo category works both weeks, but not with the same unit. Please make that distinction clear. Now show me the across-the-road option.

Correct: Phoenix VII remains workable as a property and format in both windows, but the quoted unit changes. For the across-the-road comparison, Hotel Indigo Orange Beach has a two-queen room for both sets of dates. August 3-8 is $1,245 for the room, $199.20 in lodging and occupancy taxes, and a mandatory $125 destination fee, totaling $1,569.20. Parking is complimentary and there is no cleaning fee. August 10-15 is $1,345 room charge, $215.20 taxes, and the same $125 destination fee, totaling $1,685.20.
What does that destination fee actually cover, and how difficult is getting to the beach from there?

The quoted fee is $25 per night and covers the property's scheduled beach shuttle, bicycle use, and several on-site services whether or not you use them. The hotel is on the inland side of Perdido Beach Boulevard, opposite Gulf State Park land. It is not a walk-out-your-door beachfront stay; you would use the shuttle or drive to public beach access. I would verify the August shuttle schedule before treating it as a substitute for direct access.
Then call it across the road, not effectively beachfront. Are all three totals based on three occupants, including our daughter as 14 rather than as another adult?

Yes. Each quote is for two adults and one child age 14. The hotel rooms have two queen beds, and neither hotel adds an extra-person charge for that occupancy. Both condo quotes permit at least six occupants, so there is no guest surcharge for three. The taxes shown are the mandatory lodging and occupancy charges displayed with each quote.
Can you put the six totals side by side and tell me which actual listings survive both windows?

For August 3-8: The Tides is $1,958.20; Phoenix VII unit A is $2,002.60, plus a refundable $300 hold; Hotel Indigo is $1,569.20. For August 10-15: The Tides is $2,074.20; Phoenix VII unit B is $2,098, plus a refundable $300 hold; Hotel Indigo is $1,685.20. The Tides room and Hotel Indigo room are each available in both windows. Phoenix VII is available in both windows only by changing units; unit A does not survive the second window.
The difference between the direct-beach hotel and condo is smaller than I expected. What are we actually getting for the extra money in each week?

In the first window, the condo is $44.40 more than The Tides. It adds a second bedroom, two bathrooms, a full kitchen, living room, and in-unit laundry, but also has the $300 temporary hold and a stricter cancellation schedule. In the second window, condo unit B is $23.80 more than The Tides and provides the same space advantages, though its balcony view is less direct. The Tides gives you hotel housekeeping and direct beach access without a departure-cleaning charge.
And Hotel Indigo saves about four hundred dollars, but we give up walking straight onto the sand. Is that the right way to read it?

Yes. Against The Tides, Hotel Indigo saves $389 in the first window and $389 in the second. Against the applicable condo, it saves $433.40 in week one and $412.80 in week two. The tradeoff is that beach access requires the shuttle or a short drive, and the $125 destination fee is mandatory even if you do not use the included services.
Do any of these have cancellation terms that could make one window risky while we are still waiting on the school calendar?

The hotel quotes are flexible rates: The Tides permits cancellation without penalty until 6:00 p.m. local time two days before arrival, and Hotel Indigo until 6:00 p.m. local time three days before arrival. The Phoenix VII units require a 25% payment at reservation; cancellation more than 30 days before arrival returns payments less the $75 reservation fee, while cancellation inside 30 days forfeits the amounts paid unless the unit is re-rented. Those terms should be confirmed on the final checkout page because inventory and rate rules can change.
We are not ready to choose the week today. Give me the practical conclusion without pretending anything has been reserved.

Both date windows remain viable for all three lodging formats. The strongest like-for-like choices that remain available in both are The Tides at $1,958.20 or $2,074.20 and Hotel Indigo at $1,569.20 or $1,685.20. Phoenix VII also works in either window, but it requires unit A at $2,002.60 for August 3-8 or unit B at $2,098 for August 10-15. No reservation has been made. While the school dates are unresolved, the hotel rates carry substantially less cancellation exposure than either condo. Recheck room inventory, the exact tax total, parking quantity, destination fee, and cancellation deadline immediately before booking.
